next_step: Finalize load-test plan and pricing for dedicated pool; sign SOW
notes:
Quick CRM-style summary:
- Company: Echoforge builds an AI-first contact center platform sold to mid-market telco & e-commerce CX teams. Heavy emphasis on handling large holiday spikes (Black Friday/Cyber).
- Primary ask: reliable agent-assist + ticket summarization under sudden traffic bursts. Also need tool-calls to Zendesk/SFDC without throttling.
- Current infra: hybrid (GCP + customer on-prem for PCI). They run a proprietary routing layer and expect Redwood to fit behind their VPC.
- Performance targets: baseline median generation <300ms, p95 <800ms; sustain 6k concurrent agent-assist sessions with 2x burst headroom for 30m; ticket-summarization throughput 400 docs/min during peak windows.
- Reliability needs: 99.95% success for model responses during peak events; graceful degradation acceptable (smaller model fallback) but must not drop sessions. Automatic routing to alternative region or model variant required.
- Cost posture: cost-sensitive but willing to pay for predictable dedicated capacity for peak windows. Estimated ARR range aligns with reserved capacity + ops add-ons.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required, keys in KMS/HSM, audit logging for all request/response metadata for 180 days, data residency in US and EU for different customers. Need SSO/SAML for admin console.
- Integrations: Zendesk app for tool-calls (create/update ticket), Salesforce case update, internal runbooks. Must support function/tool-calling patterns and structured outputs for automated ticket routing.
- POC plan (agreed 2026-02-15):
  - Phase 1: sandbox integration (week 1) — simple agent-assist flow + ticket summarization on sample traffic. Validate auth flows and KMS integration.
  - Phase 2: load and spike tests (week 2-3) — Redwood to run controlled synthetic bursts: 6k steady concurrent + 2x 15-minute spikes; validate latencies, autoscale behavior, fallback correctness. Provide Grafana dashboards and token-level cost reports.
  - Phase 3: smoke with real agents (week 4) — pilot with 50 agents routing real tickets for 1 week, monitor quality regression metrics and rollout canary.
- POC success criteria: p95 latency under target on steady load; fallback model maintains >85% acceptable answer rate in human evals during spikes; no unhandled session drops; audit logs visible in Console.
- Recent activity timeline:
  - 2026-01-12: Intro demo (ff_2026-01-12_echoforge-demo) — initial interest in Dedicated + Private.
  - 2026-01-28: Security questionnaire submitted; waiting SOC2 letter from Redwood.
  - 2026-02-03: Legal/data residency call — Echoforge requires US/EU tenancy split.
  - 2026-02-15: Technical spike-load call (ff_2026-02-15_spike-loadcall) — agreed on synthetic test plan; SE action items created (SUP-4128).
  - 2026-02-18: Pricing sketch delivered; Echoforge asked for committed burst windows pricing.
- Quotes / customer lines: "We cannot have the chat drop during Black Friday — even degraded answers must still flow to the agent."
- Next operational items (short): finalize SOW with committed burst windows, provide SOC2 evidence, attach detailed load-test playbook and cost estimates, legal to sign residency terms.
- Blockers restated: SOC2 letter, finalizing residency annex, exec signoff for $/month burst reserve.
- Internal notes to AE/SE: consider recommending Dedicated + Private control plane, implement request-level caching for ticket-summaries and prefix KV caching for common prompts, set up canary routing and automatic fallback policies.
- Links: PoC folder + security FAQ shared (drive links above). Jira: SUP-4128 tracking POC infra issues; INFRA-2276 for KMS integration.
